subject: Quantix - model fit recap & parity criteria
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@quantix.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ella Morris <ella.morris@quantix.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro / model fit discovery (Quantix)

Hey Irene,

Thanks for the intro call today — quick recap from our side and a few clarifying Qs so your team can prepare the trial: 

Summary of our use case:
- Customer support triage + short-answer knowledge base (internal KB + docs).
- Latency SLO: 90th <= 350ms for single-turn web UI calls (expected 60 reqs/s peak).
- Quality target: F1-style accuracy on intent/classification > 88% vs our annotated set; hallucination rate must be < 4% on sensitive doc excerpts.

What we heard from Redwood: potential to hit latency with dedicated pools + prefix caching, suggestion to trial a 7B open model + a proprietary baseline for parity checks.

Two asks before the trial kickoff: 
1) A recommended shortlist of models and why (speed vs quality tradeoffs).
2) Example prompt set and the exact benchmark links / metric definitions you will use so our data team can align.

Attached a brief dataset sample (10 examples) and our baseline eval metric definitions. Happy to get a short proposal and scheduling window for a 2-week trial.

Best,
Samir
--
Samir Patel

samir@quantix.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Intro / model fit discovery (Quantix)

Thanks Samir — great to meet you and Ella on the call. Bringing the team up to speed below and proposing concrete next steps.

Quick answers up front:
- Shortlist (recommended for trial): (1) LlamaX-7B-quant (open, 4-bit quantized) — best latency/cost balance; (2) RedCore-13B-fp16 (Redwood verified baseline) — higher quality, slightly higher latency; (3) LlamaX-13B-ft (open finetune) — mid ground, good for safety-sensitive prompts.
- We'll use your annotated set + our prompt bundle (see attached prompt_set_v1.txt) and run: accuracy (intent classification), succinctness (avg token delta), and hallucination rate (manual sampling + automated entity hallucination detector).

Proposed next steps: 
1) I’ll share a short proposal with trial scope and acceptance criteria by EOD Thu (11 Feb).
2) You send the 1k-sample benchmark (or we ingest from the shared Drive link) and we run a 3-model smoke run within 48hrs of ingest.
3) Joint evaluation call at the end of week 1 to review parity numbers and decide whether to expand to the bigger trial.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm whether the KB includes any PII that needs special handling (we can enable private deployment options if needed)?
- Any hard constraint on token limits per request?

Looping in Ben and Karthik for model selection and trial infra.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: RE: Intro / model fit discovery (Quantix)

Following up with a practical model/bench plan and what parity means operationally.

Shortlist rationale (operational):
- LlamaX-7B-quant: expect ~200-300ms p90 on a DGX-style instance with Redwood batching + KV prefix cache for short KB lookups. Good baseline to validate cost-sensitive SLA.
- RedCore-13B-fp16: our Redwood-verified baseline with tuned kernels; typically +30-60ms vs 7B but better on edge-case reasoning and lower hallucination in our internal KB tests.
- LlamaX-13B-ft: if you need stricter content controls and lower hallucination on domain-specific docs, this is the middle ground.

Parity/acceptance criteria (proposal):
1) Intent accuracy within 3 percentage points of RedCore-13B-fp16 on your annotated eval set.
2) Hallucination rate no greater than 1.5x the RedCore baseline (manual spot check + automated detector).
3) 90th latency <= 350ms for 95% of requests in the trial window (we'll measure under a synthetic 60 req/s tail).

Proposed bench artifacts we will deliver after smoke run:
- benchmark_results.csv (per-prompt model scores),
- quantx_trial_readme.md (how we ran the tests),
- short summary PDF (quantix_benchmark_summary.pdf).

Operational notes: we recommend starting on Redwood Dedicated with a small reserved pool so we can ensure stable p90 numbers; can switch to hosted for cost-savings later.

If Quantix is agreeable to the acceptance criteria above, we can schedule the trial kickoff Mon 16 Feb and deliver initial smoke results by Wed 18 Feb.

-ben

Thanks all — this is very helpful and clear. Two quick confirms from our legal/ops review: 
- KB contains internal account IDs but not consumer PII; still prefer VPC/private logging for auditability (we'll sign an SA and narrow logs).
- Token ceiling per request: 1,024 tokens (including prompt + context).

We agree to the parity definition you proposed (intent within 3pp; hallucination <= 1.5x), and we can commit to the trial kickoff on Mon 16 Feb. Please send the trial access details (API key + dedicated pool id) and we will upload the 1k eval sample to the Drive link by EOD Sun.

Also flagged the summary to our SRE to validate the synthetic 60 req/s test during week 1.

Looking forward — Ella
